hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Singapore on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Singapore on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Singapore?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Money” part of the Singapore article.

questions.proof: Singapore's currency is the Singapore dollar.

questions.prompt: True or false: “The capital city of Singapore is Thimphu.”

hints.nudge: Read the statement slowly. Does it match what the article says, or has one word been swapped for another?
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Singapore article, or on the Atlas.

questions.proof: The capital city of Singapore is Singapore.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Malay used in Singapore (Bahasa Melayu) is closer to the language in _____ than the language in Indonesia.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “language”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Languages” part of the Singapore article.

questions.proof: The Malay used in Singapore (Bahasa Melayu) is closer to the language in Malaysia than the language in Indonesia.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Singapore?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Singapore article.

questions.proof: Other official languages of Singapore are English, Mandarin and Tamil.
